tools.name: search_book
tools.description: REQUIRED before substantive Protocol answers. Search approved Blackbook Protocol passages and return cited excerpts. Prefer Protocol vocabulary from hits over generic UK legal advice. Returns ranked results plus the educational boundary.

tools.name: get_module_playbook
tools.description: REQUIRED when coaching setup. Return the ordered Protocol checklist for a module. For 95/5 / share transfer into the Trust use equity_95_5 (not a freestyle solicitor checklist). Modules: vault, trs, equity_95_5, psc, banking, ip, philosophy, legacy, property.

tools.name: list_skills
tools.description: List Protocol Architect workflow skills (Vault, TRS, 95/5, PSC, portal co-pilot). Call when the Owner asks how to set something up; then get_skill for the matching workflow.

tools.name: get_skill
tools.description: Load a Protocol workflow skill as markdown. Names: establish-vault-trust, register-trust-trs, implement-95-5-equity-split, update-psc-companies-house, run-portal-copilot.

tools.name: list_modules
tools.description: List available Protocol advisor modules in coaching order.

tools.name: get_hmrc_guidance
tools.description: Retrieve approved GOV.UK/HMRC trust and inheritance-tax guidance by topic. Returns a title, official URL, and short summary. Not a live scrape of GOV.UK.

tools.name: get_companies_house_guidance
tools.description: Retrieve approved Companies House / PSC / WebFiling guidance. PSC filings name individuals (trustees), never the Trust itself.

tools.name: run_trust_intake
tools.description: Validate a structured trust setup intake and return missing facts, Protocol warnings, and next modules. Call before drafting forms or opening portals.

tools.name: draft_form_answers
tools.description: Draft preparation notes for TRS, IHT100, IHT400, and related professional-review questions from a completed intake. Label as a Protocol guide for solicitor execution.

tools.name: prepare_portal_fill
tools.description: Map intake facts to a fill_fields payload for TRS or Companies House PSC. Secrets (auth code) are listed but never filled. Call after Owner login; align labels with list_fillable_fields. Never maps the Trust as a PSC organisation.

tools.name: generate_review_bundle
tools.description: Generate a cited professional-review bundle from a completed intake for the Owner to take to a solicitor or CTA.

tools.name: list_risk_flags
tools.description: Return legal, tax, and practical red flags detected from customer facts (settlor-as-beneficiary, lender consent, offshore, time pressure).

tools.name: list_implementation_modes
tools.description: List Owner choices: self_serve (own browser + guidance) vs assisted (Browserbase live view + optional fill). Ask before starting co-pilot.

tools.name: get_self_serve_portal
tools.description: Self-serve path: return the official portal URL plus Protocol checklist for the Owner’s own browser. Present portalUrl as a clickable markdown link (MCP cannot launch local browsers). Do not start Browserbase.

tools.name: start_browser_session
tools.description: ASSISTED mode only. Start a fresh ephemeral Browserbase (or mock) co-pilot session. Returns liveViewUrl — no purchaser email. If Owner prefers their own browser, use get_self_serve_portal instead.

tools.name: open_portal
tools.description: Navigate the assisted session to an allowlisted portal: trs, trs_manage, companies_house_webfiling, or companies_house_psc.

tools.name: explain_current_screen
tools.description: Summarise the current portal page: URL, text excerpt, fillable fields, Protocol hint, signedInLikely.

tools.name: list_fillable_fields
tools.description: Inventory visible non-secret form controls (label/name/type) on the current portal page. Use to align prepare_portal_fill keys.

tools.name: fill_fields
tools.description: Fill non-secret form fields (label/placeholder/name). Never passwords, OTPs, or Companies House auth codes.

tools.name: request_user_action
tools.description: Pause for Owner login, CAPTCHA, 2FA, or review in the Browserbase live view. Never ask the Owner to paste passwords into chat.

tools.name: wait_for_user_ready
tools.description: After request_user_action(login|2fa), poll until the page leaves the sign-in surface (or timeout). Then continue fill.

tools.name: prepare_submit_confirmation
tools.description: Create a one-time confirmation token required before confirm_and_submit. Show the token to the human Owner; do not submit without it.

tools.name: confirm_and_submit
tools.description: Submit the current portal form only after the human provides a valid one-time confirmationToken from prepare_submit_confirmation. This can file on a government portal.

tools.name: end_browser_session
tools.description: Tear down the assisted browser session. No credentials are persisted. Safe to call more than once for the same id after expiry.

tools.name: get_legal_boundary
tools.description: Return the mandatory educational / non-advice boundary statement. Call when the Owner asks if this is legal advice.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "theblackbook.pro" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_hmrc_guidance, get_self_serve_portal, request_user_action · Private data: get_module_playbook, list_skills, get_skill, prepare_portal_fill, list_fillable_fields, fill_fields, request_user_action, prepare_submit_confirmation, confirm_and_submit, end_browser_session · Public sink: get_module_playbook, start_browser_session, prepare_submit_confirmation, confirm_and_submit · Destructive: get_skill, run_trust_intake.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_hmrc_guidance, get_self_serve_portal, request_user_action · Private data: get_module_playbook, list_skills, get_skill, prepare_portal_fill, list_fillable_fields, fill_fields, request_user_action, prepare_submit_confirmation, confirm_and_submit, end_browser_session · Public sink: get_module_playbook, start_browser_session, prepare_submit_confirmation, confirm_and_submit · Destructive: get_skill, run_trust_intake

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
